title: Complete a thruster layout symmetric about both centre lines
instruction: Fit thrusters into empty nests so the layout becomes symmetric about both black centre lines, using as few thrusters as possible.
context: Reaction control thrusters are laid out symmetric about both vehicle planes, so every thruster has a twin across each plane with the same lever arm, and either axis can be commanded without coupling into the other. Two black lines stand for those planes on a 16-nest layout jig. It already holds a diagonal corner pair, which is point-symmetric and looks balanced but is symmetric about neither centre line, and one inner thruster. The work order gives the rule, not the nests. Each fitted thruster implies its mirror images about both lines, so exactly five empty nests are forced and the sixth loose thruster stays unused. Mirroring about either line alone, or completing only the inner set, fills three of the five. Nothing in the scene marks the answer: there is no model to copy and no slot pattern to fill, and an extra thruster costs as much as a missing one. The placements are plain pick and place with 5 mm of clearance per side. A 1 g bench analogue of jig work; no firing is modelled.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = +0.305. All objects are rigid and matte with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed, white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.90): the jig plate, 250 x 250 x 6 mm, edges along x and y, centred at (0.225, 0.300), spanning x 0.100 to 0.350 and y 0.175 to 0.425. Fixed, mid grey (sRGB 0.60, 0.60, 0.62): sixteen nests on the plate in a 4 x 4 grid at 65 mm pitch, centred at x 0.1275, 0.1925, 0.2575 and 0.3225 and y 0.2025, 0.2675, 0.3325 and 0.3975. Each nest is four walls 5 mm thick and 8 mm tall standing on the plate round a square pocket 34 x 34 mm: two walls 44 x 5 x 8 mm centred 19.5 mm left and right of the nest centre and two walls 5 x 34 x 8 mm centred 19.5 mm in front of and behind it. A nest is 44 mm square outside, with 21 mm of bare plate between neighbours. Fixed, black (sRGB 0.05, 0.05, 0.05): two centre lines 15 mm wide and 1 mm proud of the plate, one 250 mm long along x at y = 0.300 and one 250 mm long along y at x = 0.225, each in the 21 mm gap between the middle two rows or columns of nests, 3 mm clear of the walls on each side. Fixed, gold (sRGB 0.85, 0.65, 0.15): three fitted thrusters, cylinders 24 mm in diameter and 40 mm tall standing on the plate at the nest centres (0.1275, 0.2025), (0.3225, 0.3975) and (0.1925, 0.2675). Loose, the same gold: six identical thrusters, cylinders 24 mm in diameter and 40 mm tall, 25 g each, standing on the table in two rows, three at y = 0.120 with x 0.140, 0.200 and 0.260, and three at y = 0.490 with x 0.130, 0.190 and 0.250, 60 mm apart along each row and 55 and 65 mm from the plate edges. A loose thruster fits a pocket with 5 mm per side. The five forced nests are at (0.3225, 0.2025), (0.2575, 0.2675), (0.2575, 0.3325), (0.1925, 0.3325) and (0.1275, 0.3975); the farthest is 0.338 m from the left base. Nothing touches at the start. To build it: cut the plate from 6 mm white acrylic or plywood and tape it down; print the sixteen nests as one 8 mm tall grid, or glue 5 x 8 mm strips; lay 15 mm black tape for the two lines; glue the three fitted thrusters at their nest centres; cut the six loose thrusters from 24 mm acetal rod (about 25 g each) and paint all nine the same gold.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released and moved clear, from a top photo and a tape measure; in simulation on the final step (SCORE_OVER end). A loose thruster is seated in a nest when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), its axis is within 10 degrees of vertical (either end up), its lowest point is within 3 mm of the plate top and its centre lies inside that nest's 34 x 34 mm pocket. A thruster leaning on a wall inside a pocket (it rests at more than 30 degrees), lying across a nest, standing on the walls between nests, on a fitted or seated thruster, held above a nest, still moving, on the table or off it is seated nowhere. The three fitted thrusters and their mirror images about both lines fill eight nests; the five of those that are empty are the forced nests. R is the number of forced nests holding a seated thruster (0 to 5). X is the number of thrusters seated in any other nest. Score = max(0, R - X) / 5, so 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 or 1.0. Success, which ends the trial once it has held for 1 s, is R = 5 and X = 0: the layout is then symmetric about both lines with five thrusters, the fewest that make it so. No larger symmetric layout fits six loose thrusters (the next needs nine), so the penalty on extra thrusters is what holds the count to five. Any of the six may go to any forced nest. The start state scores 0. Reference outcomes: the corner pair taken as balanced and only the inner thruster's set completed, R = 3, 0.6; every thruster mirrored about one line only, either line, R = 3, 0.6; the corner pair taken as balanced and the inner thruster mirrored about one line, 0.2; each thruster mirrored once about each line but the inner one's double mirror at (0.2575, 0.3325) missed, R = 4, 0.8, although the layout is symmetric about neither line; all six used, five forced and one extra, 0.8; four forced and one extra, 0.6; five thrusters in random empty nests, about 0.06 on average. Pushing cannot seat a thruster: the plate stands 6 mm proud of the table and the walls 8 mm above the plate, and a tipped thruster is not upright. A value exactly on a limit passes, with a 0.1 mm margin on lengths. In simulation every test uses each thruster's centre and axis, not its axis-aligned bounds; the plate, nests, lines and fitted thrusters are static colliders. The scorer cannot see the gripper, so a thruster held perfectly still in a seated pose reads as seated; on the real rig the photo after the arm withdraws decides, and a trial in which the plate moves more than 5 mm or a fitted thruster comes loose scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the six loose thrusters back on their marks; the plate, the nests, the lines and the three fitted thrusters do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: the thrusters are plain gold cylinders 24 x 40 mm without nozzles, valves or lines, and the nests are square pockets with 5 mm per side, because the simulator's 5 mm contact offset makes tight fits unreliable. The fitted thrusters are static colliders, glued on a real rig. Rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and matte colours; no firing or plumbing is modelled. Earth gravity on a bench, which is where jig layout is done.
